QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_39

answer.text: Explaining disclosures, risk factors, product fit and investor requirements; suitability assessment; KYC facilitation; and transaction documentation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 270-271), pre-commitment services include engaging with investors, preparing pitches, providing the distribution kit (which contains KYC documentation), explaining disclosures and risk factors and product fit, advising on product/risk profile and investor fit, compiling investor information requirements, facilitating fund due diligence, seeking capital-commitment consent, and assisting transaction paperwork. The Trap: Reducing pre-investment work to cheque collection, PPM hand-off, or return guarantees ignores the distributor's suitability and disclosure obligations. Note: KYC forms are part of the distribution kit, so distributors should treat KYC facilitation as a routine, not optional, step in the onboarding workflow.
